implemented_requirements.evidence: FileHandler.read_file in file_handler.py validates the path and returns the file contents.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect palindromes (word, phrase, line, all modes)
implemented_requirements.evidence: PalindromeDetector.detect in palindrome_detector.py dispatches to _detect_word_palindromes, _detect_phrase_palindromes, and _detect_line_palindromes.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Command‑line interface with arguments (input file, mode, case‑sensitivity, punctuation handling, min length, output file)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Argument parser built in main.py (build_argument_parser) defines all required options and passes them to the detection pipeline.

report_generator.py defines ReportGenerator.generate_console_report that calls a non‑existent generate_text_report method; reportgenerator.py (different filename) defines generate_text_report but is never imported.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Write report to optional output file
implemented_requirements.evidence: run_detection in main.py writes the report using FileHandler.write_file when --output is supplied.

critical_issues: ReportGenerator imported from report_generator.py lacks a generate_text_report method; generate_console_report calls the missing method, causing an AttributeError at runtime.
A second file reportgenerator.py defines a different ReportGenerator class that references undefined attribute _SEPARATOR, leading to NameError if it were used.
The presence of two similarly named modules (report_generator.py and reportgenerator.py) creates ambiguity and prevents the intended report generation code from being executed.
judge.summary: The submitted code includes most of the required functionality: file I/O, palindrome detection across several modes, and a CLI. However, the reporting component is broken because the imported ReportGenerator class does not implement the required generate_text_report method, and an alternate implementation in a differently named file is never used and also contains errors. These critical issues make the program unlikely to run successfully, resulting in a failing verdict.
